question.text: Nilgiri Multi-Strategy Fund (Cat III AIF) reports the following monthly excess returns (fund minus Nifty 50 TRI) over five months: +1.0%, -0.5%, +0.5%, -1.0%, +1.0%. What is the annualised tracking error (using sample standard deviation of excess returns with n-1 denominator, annualised by sqrt(12))?

explanation.text: The Logic: Excess returns (%): 1.0, -0.5, 0.5, -1.0, 1.0. Mean = 0.20%. Squared deviations: (0.8)^2=0.64, (-0.7)^2=0.49, (0.3)^2=0.09, (-1.2)^2=1.44, (0.8)^2=0.64; sum = 3.30. Using sample SD (n-1 denominator): sample variance = 3.30/4 = 0.825; monthly SD = sqrt(0.825) approximately 0.9083%. Annualised TE = 0.9083% * sqrt(12) approximately 0.9083 * 3.4641 approximately 3.146%, i.e., approximately 3.10%. The Trap: Option A (~2.83%) uses population SD (divide by n) — the stem here specifies sample SD, so the n-1 form is required. Option C (8.49%) uses sqrt(12) * mean absolute excess — wrong formula. Option D (29.39%) multiplies by 12 instead of sqrt(12) — incorrect annualisation. Note: The choice between sample (n-1) and population (n) SD changes the answer; the stem specifies sample SD, so the divisor is n-1.
